text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The Council of Europe Parliamentary Assembly session elected Estonian representative Kristiina Ojuland as vice-president of the assembly. Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi defended in his speech a proposal to end CE supervision of Estonia over its Russian minority.

- The opposition is gathering strength to force the premier to resign over the apartments affair, but lacks the necessary number of votes. Meanwhile opposition leaders have called on Vahi to step down on his own.
- Centre Party leader and Tallinn city council chairman Edgar Savisaar declared that the appartments transactions in central Tallinn were illegal.

- The UNDP granted $250,000 to Estonia for the formulation of a strategic plan of sustainable development. An agreement was signed after the UNDP-Nordic conference for Central and Eastern European countries on sustainable development in the region.
- Eight MPs link high officials of the central bank with the murder of a commercial bank official last year and a major transaction of money, allegedly proceeds from the roubles sale of 1992.

- Wages due to the Oru turf plant staff have not yet been paid because of a misunderstanding over taxes. The daily and the BNS news agency have reached an agreement concerning the reporting of the situation in Oru. Eesti Paevaleht accused BNS of sensationalism and unreliable reporting on Saturday.
- Tallinn city government intends to ban all transactions with the appartments, suspected to have been privatised illegally.
- A computer hacker managed to remove more than 400,000 kroons from the account of a dairy firm.
- Norway has granted 34,000 kroons for the teaching of Estonian to police cadets.

- The daily said it is the first to publish the list of individuals and firms, who purchased Union Bank shares before its merger with the North Estonian Bank and who it says are suspected of insider dealing. The list includes several high finance ministry officials and an MP.

- An Estonian business delegation claims that the interest in Estonia showed in Singapore and Korea was remarkable. A Daewoo delegation has already visited Estonia and a Singapore business delegation is to arrive in September.
